messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for Wireless Communication without making unsupported claims?

### Short answer
To compare an R&S signaling / non-signaling wireless tester solution with a competitor without unsupported claims, use formal R&S specifications/features/order-option evidence for our products, formal competitor datasheets/release notes/support terms for the competitor products, and avoid treating internal battle-card language such as “only,” “lower TCO,” “leadership,” or “fewer boxes” as technical proof unless independently documented [3][6][27][84].
### Evidence required
- For the R&S signaling side, use CMX500 formal specifications and features evidence: CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution supporting LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD and TDD, while its features document lists NR FR1/FR2 signaling, LTE signaling, NB-IoT/NB-NTN signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput measurement, application tests, IP traffic analysis, GUI, XLAPI and SCPI [7][8].  
- For CMX500 option-level claims, cite the relevant option tables, such as WLAN signaling options CMX-KS350B/351B/352B/353B/355B/356B/357B/360B/365B, LTE signaling CMX-KS500B/M/X, NR signaling CMX-KS600B/M/X and related NR extensions [39][71][73].  
- For CMX500 specification-level claims, use the CMX500 specifications document rather than the features overview, because the knowledge base states that CMX500 specifications are the binding source and that features/functions data without tolerance limits is not binding [70].  
- For the R&S non-signaling / production side, use CMP180 formal product and specification evidence, because CMP180 is documented as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with configurable multiport RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options and R&S VSE analysis capability [22][23].  
- For CMP180 option or measurement-range claims, use CMP180 Specifications Version 08.00 and not only the Features and Functions overview, because the features document is a test-applications overview and says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be verified in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [24][55][56].  
- For CMP200 claims, use its own Features and Functions and specifications evidence, because CMP200 is a Radio Communication Tester, but its features source says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 5216.4391.22 [58][59][60].  
- For CMW500 or CMW270 claims, use the CMW data sheet and observe its stated specification conditions, because data without tolerance limits is not binding, specified performance depends on warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration cycle and internal automatic adjustments, and typical or nominal values are not guaranteed [10][13][40].  
- For competitor claims, obtain the competitor’s official datasheets, release notes, option/license information and support terms, because the Anritsu page says frequency range, bandwidth, data rate, option code, software tools and support model require Anritsu official datasheet / release notes / support terms verification [84].  
- For Anritsu MT8000A comparisons, do not cite R&S battle-card numbers such as FR2 43.5 GHz, 800 MHz bandwidth, 5 Gbps, or FR3 0.4–16 GHz to customers unless Anritsu official sources are added [35].  
- For Keysight comparisons, obtain Keysight official specifications/features documents, because the CMX500-vs-Keysight page says the battle card does not replace CMX500, CMW500 or Keysight UXM formal specifications/features documents and that Keysight claims currently come only from an R&S internal battle card [27].  
- For amarisoft comparisons, obtain amarisoft official资料 and third-party evidence, because the amarisoft comparison page says the competitor claims currently have only a single R&S internal battle-card source [6].  
- For VIAVI O-RU-related competitor comparisons, obtain VIAVI official datasheets/application notes, product names, versions, supported O-RAN WG4 spec versions, licenses and interface options, because the cited R&S sources do not provide those formal details [19][21].  
- For market-share, TCO, “only platform,” “first,” “leadership,” “widest frequency range,” “fewer boxes,” or “lower TCO” claims, provide formal evidence such as market reports, validation reports, calculations, quotes, contracts, release notes or public material, because the passages classify such wording as sales language or internal market/battle-card statements rather than verified technical specifications [3][27][28][46][48].  
- For conformance or operator-certification comparisons, provide validation reports, test case lists, PTCRB/GCF database exports or official approval criteria evidence, because the cited competitor/conformance passages note missing validation reports, test case IDs, band combinations, measurement criteria or official database evidence [28][50][52][54].  
### What is not enough
- An R&S internal battle card alone is not enough, because the CMX500-vs-Anritsu, CMX500-vs-Keysight and CMX500-vs-amarisoft pages explicitly define those pages as sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [1][4][25].  
- A features/functions document alone is not enough for guaranteed measurement limits, because CMX500, CMP180 and CMP200 feature documents are overviews and direct measurement ranges or tolerance limits back to their specifications documents [38][55][56][59][60][70].  
- A competitor weakness statement from an R&S source is not enough, because the Anritsu page says R&S battle-card weakness narratives cannot be treated as Anritsu official specifications or market facts [84].

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › 對比表
| 主題 | R&S / CMX500 positioning | Anritsu positioning | 來源限制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 架構 | one-platform architecture；FR1 + FR2 + FR3 + Wi-Fi + RF + fading | multiple RF boards、external converters、multiple boxes；另依 [[mx844030pc-j1200]]，[[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 是 software-based [[Virtual Signalling Tester]]，可用 MAC / PHY Digital-IQ / RF interfaces | battle card 未提供正式 CMX500 RFU18 或 Anritsu module datasheet；MX844030PC brochure 未提供 CMX500 比較資料 |

| Fading | integrated / native fading | external PC software / chambers / software | source 未列 option code 對照 |
| IP throughput | native high-throughput IP testing | IP Option 012 + external PC | source 未列 throughput profile 或測試條件 |

### Short answer
To compare an R&S signaling / non-signaling wireless tester solution with a competitor without unsupported claims, use formal R&S specifications/features/order-option evidence for our products, formal competitor datasheets/release notes/support terms for the competitor products, and avoid treating internal battle-card language such as “only,” “lower TCO,” “leadership,” or “fewer boxes” as technical proof unless independently documented [3][6][27][84].
### Evidence required
- For the R&S signaling side, use CMX500 formal specifications and features evidence: CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution supporting LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD and TDD, while its features document lists NR FR1/FR2 signaling, LTE signaling, NB-IoT/NB-NTN signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput measurement, application tests, IP traffic analysis, GUI, XLAPI and SCPI [7][8].  
- For CMX500 option-level claims, cite the relevant option tables, such as WLAN signaling options CMX-KS350B/351B/352B/353B/355B/356B/357B/360B/365B, LTE signaling CMX-KS500B/M/X, NR signaling CMX-KS600B/M/X and related NR extensions [39][71][73].  
- For CMX500 specification-level claims, use the CMX500 specifications document rather than the features overview, because the knowledge base states that CMX500 specifications are the binding source and that features/functions data without tolerance limits is not binding [70].  
- For the R&S non-signaling / production side, use CMP180 formal product and specification evidence, because CMP180 is documented as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with configurable multiport RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options and R&S VSE analysis capability [22][23].  
- For CMP180 option or measurement-range claims, use CMP180 Specifications Version 08.00 and not only the Features and Functions overview, because the features document is a test-applications overview and says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be verified in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [24][55][56].  
- For CMP200 claims, use its own Features and Functions and specifications evidence, because CMP200 is a Radio Communication Tester, but its features source says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 5216.4391.22 [58][59][60].  
- For CMW500 or CMW270 claims, use the CMW data sheet and observe its stated specification conditions, because data without tolerance limits is not binding, specified performance depends on warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration cycle and internal automatic adjustments, and typical or nominal values are not guaranteed [10][13][40].  
- For competitor claims, obtain the competitor’s official datasheets, release notes, option/license information and support terms, because the Anritsu page says frequency range, bandwidth, data rate, option code, software tools and support model require Anritsu official datasheet / release notes / support terms verification [84].  
- For Anritsu MT8000A comparisons, do not cite R&S battle-card numbers such as FR2 43.5 GHz, 800 MHz bandwidth, 5 Gbps, or FR3 0.4–16 GHz to customers unless Anritsu official sources are added [35].  
- For Keysight comparisons, obtain Keysight official specifications/features documents, because the CMX500-vs-Keysight page says the battle card does not replace CMX500, CMW500 or Keysight UXM formal specifications/features documents and that Keysight claims currently come only from an R&S internal battle card [27].  
- For amarisoft comparisons, obtain amarisoft official资料 and third-party evidence, because the amarisoft comparison page says the competitor claims currently have only a single R&S internal battle-card source [6].  
- For VIAVI O-RU-related competitor comparisons, obtain VIAVI official datasheets/application notes, product names, versions, supported O-RAN WG4 spec versions, licenses and interface options, because the cited R&S sources do not provide those formal details [19][21].  
- For market-share, TCO, “only platform,” “first,” “leadership,” “widest frequency range,” “fewer boxes,” or “lower TCO” claims, provide formal evidence such as market reports, validation reports, calculations, quotes, contracts, release notes or public material, because the passages classify such wording as sales language or internal market/battle-card statements rather than verified technical specifications [3][27][28][46][48].  
- For conformance or operator-certification comparisons, provide validation reports, test case lists, PTCRB/GCF database exports or official approval criteria evidence, because the cited competitor/conformance passages note missing validation reports, test case IDs, band combinations, measurement criteria or official database evidence [28][50][52][54].  
### What is not enough
- An R&S internal battle card alone is not enough, because the CMX500-vs-Anritsu, CMX500-vs-Keysight and CMX500-vs-amarisoft pages explicitly define those pages as sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [1][4][25].  
- A features/functions document alone is not enough for guaranteed measurement limits, because CMX500, CMP180 and CMP200 feature documents are overviews and direct measurement ranges or tolerance limits back to their specifications documents [38][55][56][59][60][70].  
- A competitor weakness statement from an R&S source is not enough, because the Anritsu page says R&S battle-card weakness narratives cannot be treated as Anritsu official specifications or market facts [84].
